title: WHO checklist gates knife-to-skin
logic: If an operative record is being opened for any procedure and the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist sign-in and time-out are not recorded as complete, the operative note must not proceed to the incision step.
action: Block progression of the operative record past positioning until checklist sign-in and time-out are captured; prompt the recording clinician to complete them with the theatre team.

title: Group-and-save before laparotomy
logic: If an emergency laparotomy is booked and no group-and-save or cross-match sample is recorded within the current admission, the booking is incomplete.
action: Flag the theatre booking as incomplete and prompt for blood bank sample; allow documented override by the operating surgeon for immediate life-threat cases.

title: Post-laparotomy intra-abdominal sepsis pattern
logic: If a patient between postoperative day 1 and day 7 of an abdominal operation has sustained heart rate above 100, new or worsening abdominal pain, fever, or rising early-warning score, intra-abdominal sepsis (leak, collection, ischaemia) is the presumed cause until excluded.
action: Raise a danger-sign alert to the surgical team for senior review within 1 hour; recommend septic screen and senior decision on imaging versus return to theatre; do not attribute deterioration to pain or chest infection without senior assessment.

title: Irreducible hernia with pain is strangulation until proven otherwise
logic: If a documented hernia becomes irreducible and painful, or shows overlying skin changes, or is accompanied by vomiting or obstruction, strangulation must be presumed.
action: Escalate to EMERGENCY pathway: analgesia, intravenous fluids, nasogastric tube if obstructed, and immediate surgical referral; do not schedule for an elective list.

title: High-risk patient triggers pre-operative escalation
logic: If a patient listed for intermediate or major surgery is ASA III or above, or has predicted major blood loss, or is over 65 with an emergency abdominal indication, they are classified high perioperative risk.
action: Require documented anaesthetic review before theatre, ensure blood availability, and prompt consideration of transfer to or booking at a central hospital with HDU capacity.

title: Antibiotic prophylaxis for abdominal surgery
logic: If a clean-contaminated or contaminated abdominal procedure is booked, single-dose intravenous cefazolin should be given within 60 minutes before incision, with metronidazole added whenever the gastrointestinal lumen will or may be opened; established infection converts prophylaxis to a treatment course.
action: Prompt prophylaxis agent and timing at anaesthetic induction; record administration time in the operative record; suppress the prompt when a treatment course is already charted.

title: Structured post-operative observation frequency
logic: If a patient returns from any general surgical procedure under general or spinal anaesthesia, observations (vital signs and early-warning score) are due at least hourly for the first 4 hours, then 4-hourly for 24 hours, with any score breach escalated per the early-warning protocol.
action: Generate the post-operative observation schedule on the ward task list and alert the responsible nurse when an observation is overdue or the score breaches threshold.

title: Conservative small bowel obstruction trial has a clock
logic: If adhesive small bowel obstruction is managed conservatively, nasogastric output, abdominal signs, and fluid balance must be reviewed at least 12-hourly, and failure to resolve by 48–72 hours mandates senior surgical review for operative decision.
action: Start a 72-hour review timer at diagnosis; surface 12-hourly review tasks; at 48 hours flag the case for mandatory senior surgical decision and record the decision outcome.

title: Post-operative wound and histology review
logic: If a patient is discharged after a general surgical procedure, a wound review at 7–14 days at the nearest facility is due, and any specimen sent to histology requires a documented result review and patient communication within 4 weeks.
action: Auto-book wound review follow-up on discharge; open a histology-tracking task that stays red until the result is reviewed, actioned, and communicated to the patient.
